chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Richard's last invention: a dual hydraulic and electric brake
summary: Richard spent his earnings on new inventions; his last, a backup electric brake system, came months before he died in 1965.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I saw in one of the interviews that you did you made a statement that he never really got to be wealthy, though, because he spent all the...apparently spent all the money from his inventions on the next invention he was working on.

Well, all of them do. Yeah. All of them do. He had a lot of crazy...now his last invention was...I think I've got the papers in there...I told you that (inaudible) Oh, it says here: His last invention...I got it here somewhere and his papers and everything, and I got letters where some company wanted to put it out but I turned that all over to his son when he died, you see. His last invention was that he's got a...a brake system for cars. You know you got a hydraulic brake on your car, if you got a late car, and you got your emergency. Well, now... And you got your foot brake. When the... But you haven't got the hydraulic brake. You just got your foot brake and the emergency. Well, now, if they go out you going down the hill, you just in a bad shape; but he built it so that you got...he added a hydraulic brake
and electric brake, so if one goes out, you just press a button, and you're on the other one.
Oh. That sounds like a marvelous safety feature.

Sure, it is. I got letters all in there where they wrote me and they want to...they want to handle it. See? I can show them to you if you want it, and...but I turned it over to his son. I don't know what his son done about it. This happened just six...eight months before he died.
Yeah, you never without a brake. See? If one goes out, the other one's on--automatically.
